item.title: ECB leadership: eurozone leaders back Pablo Hernandez de Cos (Spain, 55, BIS General Manager, Bank of Spain governor 2018-2024) to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president (Euronews, published 15:18 CET Thu Nov 26 = 22:18 Taipei; AP; Reuters via Investing.com citing European Council President Costa on X). Lagarde steps down Feb 7, 2027. Same package: France's Laurence Boone expected to take market operations from Isabel Schnabel (leaves Jan 3, 2027 for the IMF); Germany's Markus Brunnermeier in line to replace chief economist Philip Lane (term ends May 31, 2027). Process: EU ambassadors agreed recommendation texts; formal European Council appointment expected in December after consulting the European Parliament and ECB Governing Council. Context (Euronews): ECB raised rates twice this year; euro area inflation 4% in October. VIEWS (opinion, not fact): Jefferies' Adegbembo (to Reuters) sees de Cos as slightly more dovish than rival Klaas Knot but leadership change alone unlikely to alter the rate approach; MUFG's Cook calls him a pragmatic centrist, MUFG forecasts a 25bp hike in March. EURUSD/gold reaction attributable to the decision = UNKNOWN

item.title: USTR proposes Section 301 'structural excess capacity' tariffs on 14 economies (USTR press release dated Wed Nov 25, 2026; clock time = UNKNOWN). Determinations: China, EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, India; no determination for Mexico or Norway. Proposed maximum additional rates (alternate rate in brackets, per Sandler Travis & Rosenberg summary): China 20% (10% on certain Annex A products) [40% if consultations/commitments 'unsatisfactory']; EU 15%, terminating Dec 1 2028 [20%]; Japan 15% [20%]; South Korea 15% [25%]; Taiwan 15% [25%]; Switzerland 15% [20%]; India 25% [17%]; Vietnam 35% [20% with a reciprocal trade agreement]; Singapore 20% [10%]; Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand 18% [25%]; Cambodia 18% [25%]; Bangladesh 18% [20%]. Exemptions include Section 232 goods (steel/aluminum/copper, autos and parts, semiconductors, patented pharma, wood). These are PROPOSALS, not in effect: comments due Jan 5, public hearing Jan 25. Reuters: USTR intends to cap new tariffs at lower levels agreed in completed or ongoing trade deals. Market reaction attributable to this announcement (gold/DXY/JPY/EUR/CNH) = UNKNOWN; an X news summary links Wednesday's equity selloff to the tariff plans - attribution is that summary's view, not verified

item.title: RELEASED - Fed Beige Book, November 2026 (Federal Reserve, Wed Nov 25 14:00 ET = 03:00 Taipei Thu; prepared by Atlanta Fed, info collected on or before Nov 16). Activity: 8 of 12 Districts reported slight-to-moderate growth, 4 no change; consumer spending little changed, households price sensitive and more selective; auto sales softened (contacts cite elevated fuel prices and higher interest rates); residential real estate weakened, construction declined amid higher borrowing costs; manufacturing grew modestly; majority of Districts expect slight-to-moderate growth. Labor: employment rose slightly, hiring mostly to replace attrition; wages and benefits rose moderately - an uptick from modest in the prior report. Prices: increased moderately overall, as in the prior period; cost pressure from energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance and tariffs; input costs generally outpaced selling prices; contacts expect expenses and prices to keep rising. Media framing (Reuters headline): 'continued growth and sticky inflation' ahead of the Fed's decision on whether to raise rates (FOMC Dec 8-9). Market reaction to the release (gold/DXY/yields) = UNKNOWN (not retrieved this run)
